name: Zammer Lochputz
kurzbeschreibung: Zammer Lochputz near Landeck: Tirol's mystical gorge with 30 m high Lötzer Wasserfall, historic 1923 hydroelectric power station, Spiegelturm and suspension bridge.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Zammer Lochputz in the municipality of Zams near Landeck in the Tiroler Oberland ranks among the most spectacular and legend-shrouded natural gorges in the Eastern Alps. Situated at the foot of the prominent Venetmassiv, the wild Lötzbach has carved its way deep into the hard limestone rock over millennia, creating a fascinating rocky world. As Tirol's mystical gorge, the secured water adventure trail (Wasser-Erlebnissteig) combines rushing whitewater and cascading falls with Alpine industrial history and a centuries-old Tyrolean legendary tradition – crowned by the impressive 30-metre-high Lötzer Wasserfall.

Route & Requirements

The opening up of the natural gorge to hikers looks back on a long-standing history: travelers were already drawn to this natural phenomenon in the 19th century, before the gorge reopened in June 2004 as a modern Wasser-Erlebnissteig following extensive safety works. Right at the entrance, a cultural-historical gem awaits visitors: the heritage-listed Schaukraftwerk von 1923. As one of Tirol's oldest preserved municipal power stations, it illustrates the pioneering days of Tyrolean hydropower utilisation with historic generators and turbines. Along the secured trail, daring catwalks, suspension bridges, and tunnels lead through the narrow rocky chasm. A highlight is the walk-in Spiegelturm, where optical illusions and light reflections stage the primal power of the water. Higher up sits the historic Römerturm (Lötzturm), which houses an exciting multimedia presentation on the legend of the Zammer Lochputz: the old folk tale tells of an enchanted water nymph, a young shepherd, and a greedy blacksmith; a striking bull-head rock formation sculpted by the water still watches today like a petrified "Lochputz" over the cascades of the 30-metre-high Lötzer Wasserfall plunging into the depths.

Visit & Arrival

The Zammer Lochputz is open from early May to late October. In the peak season (July and August), the gorge opens daily from 10:00 to 17:00 (last admission 16:30); in the pre- and post-season (May/June and September/October), from Thursday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00. In midsummer, atmospheric night tours through the illuminated gorge also take place on Wednesdays from 20:00. Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €6.00, seniors (60+ years) €4.50, children (7 to 15 years) €4.50, children up to 6 years free; admission is free with the regional guest card TirolWest Card. Public transport arrival: ÖBB (Railjet or REX) to Bahnhof Landeck-Zams, from there take city bus line 1 directly to the Zams Lötz stop (a modern footbridge leads straight to the gorge entrance) or walk approx. 20 minutes from the station. By car: Inntalautobahn A12 or expressway S16, exit Landeck/Zams, follow signs to Zams and the large Zammer Lochputz car park on the main road.

Tips

Due to more than 200 steps, narrow rock tunnels, and steel grid walkways, the gorge is not barrier-free and is unsuitable for wheelchairs and strollers; ankle-high, sturdy footwear with non-slip treaded soles and a windproof jacket are strongly recommended due to the constant water spray. All visitors receive a complimentary safety helmet at the entrance. In July and August, make sure to take one of the guided evening tours when the roaring waterfalls and rock faces are magically illuminated by floodlights.
